title: Minimum Average of Smallest and Largest Elements
statement:
The array `nums` holds an even number `n` of integers. Perform the following round `n / 2` times, until `nums` is empty: take out its current smallest element and its current largest element, and write down their mean, `(smallest + largest) / 2`.

Return the smallest of the `n / 2` means you wrote down, as a floating-point number. Answers within `1e-5` of the exact value are accepted.
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating the rounds means searching the array for its minimum and maximum every time, O(n²) in total. But in sorted order the rounds are predictable: the first round takes the first and last elements, the second round the second and second-to-last, and so on. So sort once and walk two pointers inwards from both ends; each step is one round.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in increasing order.
2. Put `left` on the first index and `right` on the last; `best` starts at `Infinity`.
3. While `left < right`, compute the `average` of `nums[left]` and `nums[right]` and keep the smaller of it and `best`.
4. Move both pointers one step inwards, which removes that round's pair.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorting `[7, 8, 3, 4, 15, 13, 4, 1]` gives `[1, 3, 4, 4, 7, 8, 13, 15]`. The pairs are `(1, 15)` with average 8, `(3, 13)` with 8, `(4, 8)` with 6 and `(4, 7)` with 5.5. `best` goes 8, 8, 6, 5.5, and then `left` passes `right`, so the answer is `5.5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) besides the sort.

## Pitfalls

- In Java and C, `(a + b) / 2` on integers truncates: `(1 + 4) / 2` is 2, not 2.5. Divide by `2.0`.
- The smallest average can come from any round, not just the first or the last, so check every pair.
- Starting `best` at 0 would always return 0; start it at `Infinity` (or at the first pair's average).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left` | index of the smallest element still in play |
| `right` | index of the largest element still in play |
| `average` | the mean of this round's pair |
| `best` | the smallest average seen so far |

narration.2: Sort so that every round's smallest and largest elements sit at the two ends.
narration.3: left points at the smallest element still in play...
narration.5: No round has happened yet, so any average will be smaller than best.
narration.6: Each pass of the loop is one round; it ends when the pointers cross.
narration.7: This round removes nums[left] and nums[right]; compute their mean.
narration.8: Keep the smallest mean seen so far.
narration.9: Move past the removed smallest element...
narration.12: Every round has been recorded; return the smallest mean.
